name: Collision Chimes
description: Build a moving arrow pattern whose wall flashes match the target sequence. Each arrow moves one square per beat, reverses on a wall, and turns clockwise when it encounters another arrow. All edits happen before the film; watch the changing board and revise from the visible ledger. Solve only from screenshots and visible controls in this task webpage. Programs in an isolated agent sandbox may process screenshots and issue mouse and keyboard actions through the provided gateway. Do not access the task environment through Developer Tools, console, debugger, inspector, network or source inspection, DOM or page-state inspection, the task terminal or shell, address-bar or URL/query edits, reload/navigation, browser extensions, external applications, hidden state, or unrelated tabs.

metadata.source_notes: ART-271 records Otomata's four arrow directions, one-square beat motion, wall reversal, clockwise cell encounters, and click-to-add/cycle interaction. Collision Chimes is an original self-contained reimplementation: a fresh board, target wall-event contract, generated configurations, visible event ledger, animation, input surfaces, grader, verifier, and solver are not copied from the source page. Sound is omitted; wall flashes are authoritative.
metadata.notes: The baseline is L4, full interaction, and live runner scheduling. Full input drags the visible seed arrow and clicks placed arrows; simplified input uses an explicit add button and cycle button over the same board, cells, rules, target sequence, and beat timing. The target is a complete beat-indexed wall sequence rather than the hidden starting grid, so an equivalent configuration is valid. The task needs changing frames because wall flashes, arrow motion, and later collision turns are observed across a film, but the correct edit does not expire while the agent is delayed; it is not a real-time diagnostic.
